import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Omitting types and model cardinalities

*Reference:* [Wikipedia, Type (model theory)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Type_%28model_theory%29)
-/

namespace Types

open FirstOrder

universe u v w

/-- A partial type over `T` is a set of formulas that extends to a complete type over `T`. -/
def IsPartialType {L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}} (T : L.Theory) {α : Type w}
    (p : Set (L.Formula α)) : Prop :=
  ∃ q : T.CompleteType α, ∀ ⦃φ⦄, φ ∈ p → Language.Formula.equivSentence φ ∈ q

/-- A model omits a family of finite-arity partial types if no tuple realizes any one of them. -/
def Omits {L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}} {T : L.Theory}
    (M : FirstOrder.Language.Theory.ModelType.{u, v, max u v w} T)
    {ι : Type w} (arity : ι → ℕ)
    (p : ∀ i, Set (L.Formula (Fin (arity i)))) : Prop :=
  ∀ i, ¬∃ a : Fin (arity i) → M, ∀ φ ∈ p i, φ.Realize a

/--
Assume `K` is the class of models of a first-order theory in a countable language that
simultaneously omit a countable family of partial or complete types over the empty set, each in
finitely many variables.
If `K` has a model of cardinality $\aleph_{\omega_1}$, does it have a model of cardinality
$2^{\aleph_0}$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem types :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∀ {L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}} [Countable L.Symbols] {T : L.Theory}
        {ι : Type w} [Countable ι] (arity : ι → ℕ)
        (p : ∀ i, Set (L.Formula (Fin (arity i)))),
        (∀ i, IsPartialType T (p i)) →
        (∃ M : FirstOrder.Language.Theory.ModelType.{u, v, max u v w} T,
          Omits M arity p ∧ Cardinal.mk M = Cardinal.aleph (Ordinal.omega 1)) →
        ∃ M : FirstOrder.Language.Theory.ModelType.{u, v, max u v w} T,
          Omits M arity p ∧ Cardinal.mk M = Cardinal.continuum := by
  sorry

end Types
modeling_decisions: Interpreted “countable first order theory” as an arbitrary theory in a countable first-order language, represented by `Countable L.Symbols`; in such a language the collection of sentences, and hence every theory, is countable.
Represented the countable family using an arbitrary index type with a `Countable` instance, so finite and empty families are included as well as countably infinite families.
Allowed each type its own finite arity `Fin (arity i)` and used parameter-free `L.Formula` objects, matching types over the empty set in finitely many free variables.
Modeled a partial type over `T` as a set of formulas extendable to a Mathlib `T.CompleteType`; this expresses joint consistency with `T` and includes complete as well as partial types.
Defined simultaneous omission literally: for every indexed type there is no tuple satisfying all formulas in that type.
Used Mathlib bundled nonempty models `Theory.ModelType` and exact cardinal equalities with `Cardinal.aleph (Ordinal.omega 1)` for ℵ_{ω₁} and `Cardinal.continuum` for 2^{ℵ₀}.
Followed the literal statement and did not add an “absolutely generated” or other stronger model condition that the source may have intended.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Models of cardinality continuum for theories omitting types

Let `K` be the class of models of a countable first-order theory omitting countably many types.
If `K` has a model of cardinality $\aleph_{\omega_1}$, does `K` have a model of cardinality
continuum?

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics#Model_theory_and_formal_languages)
- [Wikipedia, Type (model theory)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Type_%28model_theory%29)
- S. Shelah, *Borel sets with large squares*, Fund. Math. 159 (1999), 1–50.
  [arXiv:math/9802134](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9802134)
-/

namespace Types

open FirstOrder Language Cardinal Ordinal

universe u v w

variable {L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}} {α : Type*}

/-- An `L`-structure `M` *omits* a set `p` of `L`-formulas in the free variables `α`
(a partial type over the empty set) if no tuple of `M` realizes all the formulas of `p`. -/
def Omits (M : Type w) [L.Structure M] (p : Set (L.Formula α)) : Prop :=
  ∀ v : α → M, ∃ φ ∈ p, ¬ φ.Realize v

/-- Every structure omits the set of formulas `{⊥}`. -/
@[category test, AMS 3]
theorem omits_singleton_bot (M : Type w) [L.Structure M] :
    Omits M ({⊥} : Set (L.Formula α)) :=
  fun _ => ⟨⊥, rfl, by simp [Formula.Realize]⟩

/-- No structure omits the empty set of formulas in no free variables. -/
@[category test, AMS 3]
theorem not_omits_empty (M : Type w) [L.Structure M] :
    ¬ Omits M (∅ : Set (L.Formula (Fin 0))) :=
  fun h => by simpa using h finZeroElim

/-- A structure omits the empty set of formulas iff there are no tuples of the relevant shape. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem omits_empty_iff (M : Type w) [L.Structure M] :
    Omits M (∅ : Set (L.Formula α)) ↔ IsEmpty (α → M) := by
  simp [Omits, isEmpty_iff]

/--
Let $L$ be a countable first-order language, $T$ an $L$-theory and $S$ a countable set of
types over the empty set, i.e. sets of $L$-formulas in finitely many free variables
$x_0, \ldots, x_{n-1}$ (complete or partial). Let $K$ be the class of models of $T$ omitting
every type in $S$.

If $K$ has a model of cardinality $\aleph_{\omega_1}$, does it have a model of cardinality
continuum $2^{\aleph_0}$?

Note that for $2^{\aleph_0} \le \aleph_{\omega_1}$ the answer is positive by the downward
Löwenheim–Skolem theorem, so the question is about the case $2^{\aleph_0} > \aleph_{\omega_1}$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem types :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∀ (L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}) [Countable L.Symbols] (T : L.Theory)
        (S : Set (Σ n : ℕ, Set (L.Formula (Fin n)))), S.Countable →
        (∃ M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T, (∀ p ∈ S, Omits M p.2) ∧ #M = ℵ_ ω₁) →
        ∃ M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T, (∀ p ∈ S, Omits M p.2) ∧ #M = 𝔠 := by
  sorry

end Types
attempts.decomposition_objections: The note's claim that the literal statement follows from Morley's omitting-types theorem plus downward Löwenheim–Skolem is not correct in general: Morley's theorem needs a model of size ≥ ℶ_{ω₁}, and downward LS only settles the case 2^{ℵ₀} ≤ ℵ_{ω₁}; the case 2^{ℵ₀} > ℵ_{ω₁} is exactly what Shelah asks about. This does not affect the formalization, which follows the statement as posed with answer(True) meaning 'yes'.
modeling_decisions: `Countable L.Symbols` encodes 'countable first order theory' (a theory in a countable language); `T : L.Theory` is otherwise arbitrary (any theory in a countable language is countable).

A 'type' is modelled as a set of `L`-formulas in the free variables `Fin n` (partial or complete, over the empty set), bundled as `Σ n : ℕ, Set (L.Formula (Fin n))`; the family is a set `S` of such with `S.Countable` (so finite/empty families are allowed). No finite-satisfiability/consistency condition is imposed on the members of `S`: a set of formulas inconsistent with `T` is omitted by every model of `T`, so dropping such members does not change the class `K`, and the universally quantified statement is equivalent to the one restricted to genuine types.
`K` is represented as the models `M : Theory.ModelType T` with `∀ p ∈ S, Omits M p.2`; `Omits M p` means no tuple `v : Fin n → M` realizes every formula of `p` (Mathlib's `Formula.Realize`).
ℵ_{ω₁} is `ℵ_ ω₁ = Cardinal.aleph (Ordinal.omega 1)` (Mathlib's `aleph` indexes infinite cardinals, so this is ℵ_{ω₁} = sup_{α<ω₁} ℵ_α); continuum is `Cardinal.continuum` (`𝔠 = 2^ℵ₀`).

Models are quantified over `Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T` with fixed but arbitrary universes `u v w` (the theorem is universe-polymorphic); since the language is countable, structures of any given cardinality exist in any universe, so this does not change the mathematical content. Both the hypothesis and the conclusion range over the same universe of carriers.
Yes/no question formalized in the repository style `answer(sorry) ↔ P`, so `answer(True)` means 'yes, K always has a model of cardinality continuum'.

The docstring records the (standard) observation that the case 2^{ℵ₀} ≤ ℵ_{ω₁} is trivial by downward Löwenheim–Skolem; the formal statement itself follows the entry as posed and does not assume anything about the size of the continuum.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Types

*References:*

- [Wikipedia, Type (model theory)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Type_%28model_theory%29)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)

namespace Types

open FirstOrder

/-- A set of first-order formulas whose free variables form a finite tuple. -/
def FormulaType (L : FirstOrder.Language) :=
  Σ n : ℕ, Set (L.Formula (Fin n))

/-- A model omits a formula type if no tuple in the model realizes all its formulas. -/
def Omits {L : FirstOrder.Language} {T : L.Theory}
    (M : T.ModelType) (p : FormulaType L) : Prop :=
  ∀ v : Fin p.1 → M, ∃ φ ∈ p.2, ¬φ.Realize v

/--
Is the following true? For every countable first-order language, theory $T$, and countable
family of types over the empty set in finitely many variables: if there is a model of $T$ of
cardinality $\aleph_{\omega_1}$ omitting every type in the family, then there is such a model
of cardinality continuum?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem types : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ {L : FirstOrder.Language} (_ : Countable L.Symbols) (T : L.Theory)
      (ι : Type) (_ : Countable ι) (p : ι → FormulaType L),
      (∃ M : T.ModelType,
        Cardinal.mk M = Cardinal.aleph (Ordinal.omega 1) ∧ ∀ i, Omits M (p i)) →
      ∃ M : T.ModelType,
        Cardinal.mk M = Cardinal.continuum ∧ ∀ i, Omits M (p i) := by
  sorry

end Types
modeling_decisions: Interpreted “countable first order theory” as a theory in a countable first-order language, represented by `Countable L.Symbols`; no separate countability hypothesis on `T` is needed because every set of sentences in a countable language is countable.

Represented a type over the empty set as a set of `L.Formula (Fin n)` for some finite arity `n`. This accommodates both partial and complete types as requested; formula sets inconsistent with `T` are automatically omitted and impose no additional restriction.
Represented “countably many types” by a family indexed by an arbitrary countable type `ι`, thereby including empty, finite, and countably infinite families directly.
Used Mathlib's bundled nonempty `T.ModelType` for models of `T`, and required every model witness to omit every member of the same family simultaneously.

Read `aleph_{omega_1}` literally as `Cardinal.aleph (Ordinal.omega 1)` and continuum as `Cardinal.continuum`, without adding the stronger “absolutely generated” condition mentioned as a possible intended variant in the decomposition notes.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Omitting types: models of cardinality $\aleph_{\omega_1}$ and of cardinality continuum

Let $K$ be the class of models of a countable first-order theory $T$ that omit a given
countable family of types. If $K$ has a model of cardinality $\aleph_{\omega_1}$, does $K$ have
a model of cardinality continuum?

Here a *type* is a set of $L$-formulas over the empty set of parameters whose free variables
lie among finitely many given variables $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ (complete or partial), and a
structure *omits* a type if no tuple of its elements realizes all formulas of the type at once.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Type (model theory)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Type_%28model_theory%29)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [S. Shelah, *Borel sets with large squares*, Fund. Math. 159 (1999), 1–50](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9802134)
-/

namespace Types

open Cardinal Ordinal FirstOrder Language

universe u v w

variable {L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}} {α : Type*}

/-- An `L`-structure `M` *omits* a set of formulas `p` in the free variables `α` (a type over
the empty set of parameters) if no assignment `v : α → M` of the free variables realizes every
formula of `p` simultaneously. -/
def Omits (M : Type w) [L.Structure M] (p : Set (L.Formula α)) : Prop :=
  ¬ ∃ v : α → M, ∀ φ ∈ p, φ.Realize v

@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem omits_iff (M : Type w) [L.Structure M] (p : Set (L.Formula α)) :
    Omits M p ↔ ∀ v : α → M, ∃ φ ∈ p, ¬ φ.Realize v := by
  simp [Omits]

/-- Every structure omits the inconsistent type `{⊥}`. -/
@[category test, AMS 3]
theorem omits_singleton_bot (M : Type w) [L.Structure M] :
    Omits M ({⊥} : Set (L.Formula α)) := by
  simp [Omits]

/-- A nonempty structure does not omit the empty type. -/
@[category test, AMS 3]
theorem not_omits_empty (M : Type w) [L.Structure M] [Nonempty M] :
    ¬ Omits M (∅ : Set (L.Formula α)) := by
  simp [Omits]

/--
Let $L$ be a countable first-order language, $T$ an $L$-theory and $\Gamma$ a countable family of
types over the empty set, each in finitely many free variables. Let $K$ be the class of models of
$T$ omitting every type in $\Gamma$. If $K$ has a model of cardinality $\aleph_{\omega_1}$, does
$K$ have a model of cardinality continuum $2^{\aleph_0}$?

Here `answer(True)` means that the answer is "yes" for every such $L$, $T$ and $\Gamma$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem types :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∀ (L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}) [Countable L.Symbols] (T : L.Theory)
        (Γ : Set (Σ n : ℕ, Set (L.Formula (Fin n)))), Γ.Countable →
        (∃ M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T, (∀ p ∈ Γ, Omits M p.2) ∧ #M = ℵ_ ω₁) →
        ∃ M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T, (∀ p ∈ Γ, Omits M p.2) ∧ #M = 𝔠 := by
  sorry

end Types
attempts.decomposition_objections: None about the slot structure (a single yes/no question is correct). Minor caveat already acknowledged in the table's notes: the literal statement seems to be a known theorem (Morley's omitting-types theorem + downward Löwenheim–Skolem), whereas the cited Shelah paper asks a stronger, 'absolute' version that has no clean first-order formulation; I followed the table's instruction to formalize the statement as posed.
modeling_decisions: 'Countable first order theory' is modeled as a theory in a countable language (`Countable L.Symbols`, the same idiom as `Wikipedia/VaughtConjecture.lean`); since a countable language has only countably many sentences, every `L.Theory` is then automatically countable, so no separate countability hypothesis on `T` is stated.

'Countably many types' is modeled as a countable set `Γ : Set (Σ n : ℕ, Set (L.Formula (Fin n)))` of pairs (n, set of formulas with free variables among x_0..x_{n-1}); types are over the empty parameter set and may be partial or complete, as the decomposition notes prescribe. Sets that are not finitely satisfiable with T (hence not 'types' in the strict sense) are allowed; they are omitted by every model, so the class K is unchanged and the statement is equivalent to one restricted to genuine types.
'Omitting' is modeled as: no tuple `v : Fin n → M` realizes every formula of the type. For n = 0 the unique empty tuple makes this 'M fails some sentence of p', the correct degenerate case.

Models are taken as `T.ModelType` (nonempty structures satisfying T) in an arbitrary universe `w`, the same universe for the hypothesis and the conclusion; cardinalities are exact equalities `#M = ℵ_ ω₁` (= `Cardinal.aleph (Ordinal.omega 1)`) and `#M = 𝔠` (= `Cardinal.continuum`), as in the statement.

Following the decomposition table, the statement is formalized literally as posed on Wikipedia, with `answer(True)` meaning 'yes'. Reviewer note (kept out of the Lean file per AGENTS.md): read literally, the answer 'yes' appears to be a ZFC theorem (downward Löwenheim–Skolem preserves omitted types, and Morley's omitting-types Hanf-number theorem then gives models in every infinite cardinality); Shelah's actual question in 'Borel sets with large squares' concerns a model of size continuum obtained in a 'nice/absolute' way. The category is nonetheless `research open`, matching the status given.

The module docstring cites the Wikipedia 'Type (model theory)' article (required), the Wikipedia list page, and Shelah's paper via its arXiv page (math/9802134) rather than a DOI, to avoid a possibly broken link (no network access to verify).

first-order formulas whose free variables lie among $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$. A structure
$\mathcal{M}$ *omits* the type if no $n$-tuple of elements of $\mathcal{M}$ satisfies every

universe u v w

open Cardinal FirstOrder.Language
open scoped Ordinal

namespace Types

variable {L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}}

/-- A structure `M` *omits* the (partial) type `p`, a set of `L`-formulas in the free variables
`x_0, …, x_{n-1}`, if no `n`-tuple of elements of `M` satisfies every formula in `p`. -/
def Omits (M : Type*) [L.Structure M] {n : ℕ} (p : Set (L.Formula (Fin n))) : Prop :=
  ¬ ∃ v : Fin n → M, ∀ φ ∈ p, φ.Realize v

/-- The class `K` of models of the theory `T` that omit every type in the family `Γ`.
Each member of `Γ` is a type in some finite number `n` of free variables. -/
def modelsOmitting (T : L.Theory) (Γ : Set (Σ n : ℕ, Set (L.Formula (Fin n)))) :
    Set (Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T) :=
  {M | ∀ p ∈ Γ, Omits M p.2}

/-- Every structure omits the inconsistent type `{⊥}`. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem omits_singleton_bot (M : Type*) [L.Structure M] (n : ℕ) :
    Omits M ({⊥} : Set (L.Formula (Fin n))) := by
  simp [Omits]

/-- No nonempty structure omits the empty type. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem not_omits_empty (M : Type*) [L.Structure M] [Nonempty M] (n : ℕ) :
    ¬ Omits M (∅ : Set (L.Formula (Fin n))) := by
  simp [Omits]

/-- Every model of `T` belongs to the class of models of `T` omitting no types. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem mem_modelsOmitting_empty (T : L.Theory) (M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T) :
    M ∈ modelsOmitting T ∅ := by
  simp [modelsOmitting]

types. If $K$ has a model of cardinality $\aleph_{\omega_1}$, does it have a model of cardinality
continuum $2^{\aleph_0}$?

Here a countable first order theory is a theory in a language with countably many symbols, and
a type is any set of formulas (over the empty set) in finitely many free variables, complete
or partial.
-/

      ∃ M ∈ modelsOmitting.{u, v, w} T Γ, #M = 𝔠 := by
  sorry

end Types

  simp [Omits]

namespace Types

open FirstOrder
open FirstOrder.Language
open scoped Cardinal Ordinal

/-- A partial type over the empty set: a set of formulas in some fixed finite number of free
variables. -/
structure PartialType (L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}) where
  arity : ℕ
  formulas : Set (L.Formula (Fin arity))

namespace PartialType

/-- A partial type is a type for `T` if each of its finite subsets is realized in a model of
`T`. -/
def IsType {L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}} (p : PartialType L) (T : L.Theory) : Prop :=
  ∀ s : Finset (L.Formula (Fin p.arity)), (s : Set _) ⊆ p.formulas →
    ∃ M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, max u v} T, ∃ x : Fin p.arity → M,
      ∀ φ ∈ s, φ.Realize x

/-- A partial type is realized in a structure if one tuple simultaneously satisfies all of its
formulas. -/
def IsRealized {L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}} (p : PartialType L) (M : Type w)
    [L.Structure M] : Prop :=
  ∃ x : Fin p.arity → M, ∀ φ ∈ p.formulas, φ.Realize x

end PartialType

countable family of finite-arity types over the empty set. If $K$ contains a model of cardinality
$\aleph_{\omega_1}$, must it contain a model of cardinality continuum?

theorem types :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∀ (L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}) (_ : Countable L.Symbols) (T : L.Theory)
        (P : Set (PartialType L)), P.Countable → (∀ p ∈ P, p.IsType T) →
        (∃ M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, max u v} T,
          #M = ℵ_ ω₁ ∧ ∀ p ∈ P, ¬p.IsRealized M) →
        ∃ M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, max u v} T,
          #M = Cardinal.continuum ∧ ∀ p ∈ P, ¬p.IsRealized M := by
  sorry

end Types
modeling_decisions: Read “countable first order theory” as an arbitrary theory in a countable first-order language, following the fixed decomposition; countability of `L.Symbols` makes the available formulas, and hence every set of axioms, countable.
Represented the countable family as a `Set` satisfying `Set.Countable`, rather than an ℕ-indexed sequence, so finite and empty families are included without adding artificial repeated types.
Represented a type over the empty set as a set of `L.Formula (Fin n)` for some finite arity `n`; this includes partial types, with complete types as a special case.

Required each stated type to be finitely satisfiable together with `T`, which is the standard consistency condition for a partial type over a theory. Different finite subsets may use different models, equivalently by compactness to consistency of the full type with `T`.

A model omits a type exactly when no tuple of the specified finite arity simultaneously realizes every formula in that type; the same simultaneous omission condition is imposed on the large model and the continuum-sized model.
Used Mathlib’s bundled nonempty `Theory.ModelType` for models, `ℵ_ ω₁` for `Cardinal.aleph` indexed by the first uncountable ordinal, and `Cardinal.continuum` for the continuum.
Formalized the source’s yes/no wording with `answer(sorry) ↔ ...`; a positive answer is therefore `True`, as required by the decomposition.

new_definitions.closest_existing_considered: `FirstOrder.Language.Theory.CompleteType`, which only represents complete types and explicitly has a TODO to connect complete types to sets of formulas.
new_definitions.name: Types.PartialType
new_definitions.why_needed: The conjecture allows partial types in varying finite arities over the empty set, represented as sets of formulas. Mathlib has no such object.

new_definitions.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib’s satisfiability and `Theory.CompleteType` APIs; neither supplies a predicate for a partial set of finite-arity formulas over a theory.
new_definitions.name: Types.PartialType.IsType
new_definitions.why_needed: A raw set of formulas must be constrained to be a type consistent with the ambient theory; this predicate expresses finite satisfiability with `T`.

new_definitions.closest_existing_considered: `FirstOrder.Language.Theory.realizedTypes`, which applies only to Mathlib complete types, not partial sets of formulas.
new_definitions.name: Types.PartialType.IsRealized
new_definitions.why_needed: Omission of a partial type requires saying that no tuple satisfies all formulas in its underlying set.

statement_blocks.types:
/--
Let $K$ be the class of models of a countable first-order theory that simultaneously omit a
countable family of finite-arity types over the empty set. If $K$ contains a model of cardinality
$\aleph_{\omega_1}$, must it contain a model of cardinality continuum?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem types :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∀ (L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}) (_ : Countable L.Symbols) (T : L.Theory)
        (P : Set (PartialType L)), P.Countable → (∀ p ∈ P, p.IsType T) →
        (∃ M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, max u v} T,
          #M = ℵ_ ω₁ ∧ ∀ p ∈ P, ¬p.IsRealized M) →
        ∃ M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, max u v} T,
          #M = Cardinal.continuum ∧ ∀ p ∈ P, ¬p.IsRealized M := by
  sorry
